svg.title: One approved supplier export needs both S3 and KMS permission
svg.desc: The owner binds an approved minimal export to its recipient, exact S3 version and digest. A temporary supplier workload role must pass an S3 gate involving supplier IAM and owner bucket policy, and a separate KMS gate involving supplier IAM and owner key policy. Applicable denies and endpoint rules can still block the request. Only then can the supplier application receive bytes. Its own user authorization and copy retention remain separate. Revoking future reads cannot recall an earlier copy. Design only; no live test.
svg.text: A supplier needs parts and quantities, not customer data.
A version ID alone is not content approval.
Supplier uses a temporary workload role
No shared long-lived key or employee sign-in.
Gate 1 · Can it read this S3 version?
An unversioned grant can defeat the limit.
Gate 2 · Can S3 use the KMS key?
Check the actual SSE-KMS service path.
Approved bytes reach the supplier app
Its users and copy retention need own controls.
Deny/endpoint rules may still block a read. A past copy
cannot be recalled. Design only; no AWS test here.
